findings.message:
[P1] Rate-limit password step-up attempts

The new `/api/auth/step-up/password` route calls `verifyPassword` on every request without the existing `allowPasswordAttempt` limits. An authenticated caller with a stolen session and CSRF can make unlimited guesses against the account password, and any session can repeatedly trigger 600,000-iteration PBKDF2 work to exhaust worker CPU. Reuse the per-source and per-account password budgets before verification.

src/passport.ts:1065-1070

[P2] Wire shipped clients to the step-up endpoints

These routes are only exercised by tests. None of `public/auth.js`, `device.js`, `agent_tokens.js`, `admin_users.js`, or `admin_projects.js` calls `/api/auth/step-up/password|start|finish` or sends `x-step-up-token`; the device page does not even bootstrap a CSRF token. Once `recentAuthAt` ages out, the shipped pages receive 401 `reauthentication_required` for password changes, passkey removal, device approval, and administrator writes and render it as a dead session or generic failure, so the requested step-up cannot be completed from the product UI. Add a shared password/passkey step-up flow, or an explicit re-login fallback, before enforcing the gate globally.

src/passport.ts:3411-3418

summary: Server-side step-up enforcement is implemented and the task regressions are present, but the new password verifier lacks attempt limiting and the shipped UI has no step-up handshake.

evidence: `requireSensitiveAuth` checks an operation and target-bound one-use token or a five-minute `recentAuthAt` window at `src/passport.ts:723-762`, and `grantHubStepUpAuthorization` plus `consumeHubStepUpAuthorization` implement hashed session-bound tokens in `src/auth_store.ts:1553-1613`.
Sensitive password, passkey, agent-token, agent-approval, and administrator handlers call `requireSensitiveAuth` before the write and invalidate pending authorizations after successful changes.

Regressions in `tests/bun_test.ts:1537-1794`, `src/handler_test.ts:378-591`, and `tests/passport_cutover_test.ts:859-1039` cover stale-session plus CSRF rejection, operation and target mismatch, session mismatch, one-use replay, and post-use invalidation.
The password and passkey step-up endpoints accept only the current account password or a current owner credential, require CSRF on credential collection, and expire authorizations after five minutes.
